Continue building Trueup in this repository. Read README.md, hackathon.md, CHANGELOG.md and src/ first. This session is recorded by Entire and published: work only inside this repository and never mention anything outside it. Do not git commit or push.

Task: the comparer and the reports (pure core, no I/O, fully unit tested).
1. `src/trueup/core/compare.py`: given an Observation (truth from the fake's log + app outcome, trace = exported spans), apply these checks and return Mismatches with severity:
   - Run status: app raised / got a result -> top-level span ERROR / not ERROR. HIGH if a crash shows OK at the top level.
   - Call status: provider returned an error or the stream failed -> that LLM span ERROR with an exception event. MEDIUM.
   - Call count: provider requests logged -> one LLM span per request. HIGH if duplicated or missing.
   - Tokens: provider usage -> per-span tokens equal and the sum over LLM spans equals the real sum. HIGH if the sum is off. Only compare when the fake actually sent usage.
   - Output: text / refusal / tool calls the app received -> recorded on the span, tool args exact. MEDIUM.
   - Finish: finish reason / response status recorded; failed/incomplete visible. MEDIUM.
   - Span closed: call ended -> span ended and exported. HIGH if a call disappears.
   Severity rule: HIGH changes a number or status a dashboard shows by default (run status, cost, call count); MEDIUM is wrong or missing detail in a span; LOW is extra or cosmetic.
   Each library names attributes differently (neatlogs, OpenInference `llm.*`/`openinference.*`, OpenLLMetry `gen_ai.*`/`llm.*`): put the attribute mapping in one small adapter per library, data-driven, and test each adapter against real span JSON saved from the sweeps in `.trueup/runs/` (copy a few small samples into `tests/fixtures/`, no secrets in them).
   Where truth was changed by the library itself (e.g. a library adding stream_options.include_usage), compare against what the provider really sent, and record that the library changed the request as a LOW note, not a bug.
2. Leads: a mismatch is a "lead" (never called a bug here). `trueup sweep <lib>` now runs the comparer and prints a table: scenario, check, expected, actual, severity; writes `leads.json`; exits 1 if any lead, 0 if none, 2 if it could not run.
3. `trueup audit <agent.py>`: run a user's script's `main()` under each plain-SDK scenario with the fake provider via env base URLs (OPENAI_BASE_URL / ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL) and the chosen tracing library, then compare. Keep it simple and honest; document limits.
4. Re-run the sweeps for all three libraries (one at a time, memory is limited) and save the leads. Write the counts per library and per check into hackathon.md. Do not describe any lead as a confirmed bug; the self-check comes next.
5. Update CHANGELOG.md. Plain words, no filler. Run `uv run pytest -q`. Finish with a summary: tests, leads per library by severity, anything not done.

Trueup finds where your AI agent's traces disagree with what really happened, fixes the tracing code, and proves the fix.

## What it does

Teams watch their AI agents through tracing libraries such as neatlogs, OpenInference and OpenLLMetry. These libraries wrap the AI provider's SDK and record each call. When a wrapper gets a case wrong, the dashboard can show a crashed run as OK, miss a refusal, or show twice the real cost.

Trueup runs the agent against a fake provider, so it knows what really happened. It captures what the trace says and compares the two. When they disagree, it looks for the cause in the tracing library, writes a fix with a test, and checks that the fix works.

The work is split into small workers: planner, runner, comparer, checker, deduper, fixer, verifier and reporter. A language model proposes; plain code decides.

## Status: early build

`trueup doctor` and `trueup sweep <neatlogs|openinference|openllmetry>` work. `sweep` runs the plain-SDK scenarios against a fake provider and writes truth and trace to `.trueup/runs/<run_id>/`. It does not compare them yet. The other commands (`audit`, `fix`, `upstream`, `verify`, `report`) print "not built yet" and exit 2.

Exit codes: 0 no mismatches, 1 mismatches found, 2 could not run.

## Run it

Needs Python 3.12 and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/).

```sh
uv sync
uv run trueup doctor
uv run pytest -q         # offline unit tests
uv run pytest -q -m e2e  # builds per-library venvs, runs subprocesses
uv run trueup sweep neatlogs
```

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
# Build log

neatHack, 10-12 Oct 2026.

## 2026-10-10: skeleton

- Set up the uv project (Python 3.12, src layout) with the `trueup` command.
- Added the data model in `trueup.core`: Observation, Mismatch, Run, Finding and Severity, each with `to_dict`/`from_dict`.
- `trueup doctor` reports the Python version and whether the two keys are set, without printing them. Other commands exit 2 with "not built yet".
- Tests for the round trip, severity order and doctor. CI runs them on push.
- Nothing is audited yet. No findings so far.

## 2026-10-10: the truth side

- `trueup.fake`: a local fake provider (stdlib http.server in a thread, random free port). It speaks OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages. The request's model name picks the scenario: plain, streamed with and without usage, two parallel tool calls with split streamed arguments, refusal, n=2, HTTP 500 and 529, error event mid-stream, status failed and incomplete, reasoning summary, thinking, tool_use with input_json_delta, and a dropped connection. Every id is unique per call and per fake instance. The truth log records each request and what was sent back, including tokens per call, or that no usage was sent.
- 34 fixture tests run the real `openai` and `anthropic` SDKs against the fake. Two SDK behaviours we found and recorded: the openai SDK passes a Responses `error` event to the app instead of raising, and the anthropic SDK lets a dropped stream through as a raw `RemoteProtocolError`, not an SDK exception.
- `trueup.scenarios`: 31 plain-SDK scenarios as data (chat 12, Responses 9, Anthropic 10), each with expected truth. A unit test runs every app with no tracing library and checks the expectations against what really happens. That check caught one wrong expectation (streamed tool calls without include_usage carry no tokens). 20 LangChain/LangGraph/OpenAI Agents cases are listed as not_built.
- `trueup.runner`: runs one scenario in a fresh subprocess in `.trueup/venvs/<lib>` (built with uv), using the library's recommended setup and an in-memory span exporter. It returns truth plus spans as JSON. A scenario that cannot run is reported NOT RUN with the reason.
- Regression tests for four traps: reused response ids, a reused async client across asyncio.run, a missing-usage reply read as a bug, and neatlogs exporting to a dead endpoint.
- `trueup sweep <library>` writes observations and `summary.txt` to `.trueup/runs/<run_id>/`. All three libraries ran 31/31. The first openllmetry sweep was 0/31 NOT RUN because `traceloop-sdk` imports `httpx` without declaring it; we now install `httpx` in that venv.
- Leads for the comparer (not judged yet): neatlogs adds `stream_options.include_usage` to the app's streamed chat request. openinference exports no span for a stream closed early, or for a Responses stream that ends with an error event. openllmetry marks chat streams that raised (error event, cut) as OK, and exports no span for Responses failed/incomplete or for Anthropic stream errors and cuts.
# Changelog

## Unreleased

- Fake provider (`trueup.fake`) for OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses and Anthropic Messages, with a truth log.
- Scenario library (`trueup.scenarios`): 31 plain-SDK scenarios; framework scenarios listed as not built.
- Runner (`trueup.runner`): one scenario per subprocess in a per-library uv venv (neatlogs, openinference, openllmetry), spans captured in memory.
- `trueup sweep <library>` writes observations to `.trueup/runs/<run_id>/`.
- Dev dependencies: `openai`, `anthropic`. Tests that spawn subprocesses are marked `e2e` and excluded by default.
- Project skeleton: uv project, `trueup` command, data model in `trueup.core`, `doctor` command, tests and CI.

"""Runs one scenario under one library. Executed in a fresh subprocess.

python -m trueup.runner.child <library> <scenario_id> <out.json>
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import gc
import json
import logging
import sys
import time
import traceback
from importlib import metadata
from typing import Any

from trueup.fake import FakeProvider
from trueup.runner import truth
from trueup.runner.apps import APPS
from trueup.runner.setups import SETUPS, VERSIONED
from trueup.scenarios import get

ATTR_MAX = 2000


def _value(v: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(v, (tuple, list)):
        return [_value(x) for x in v]
    if isinstance(v, str) and len(v) > ATTR_MAX:
        return v[:ATTR_MAX] + f"...[{len(v) - ATTR_MAX} more chars]"
    return v


def span_to_dict(s: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    ctx = s.get_span_context()
    return {
        "name": s.name,
        "kind": s.kind.name,
        "trace_id": format(ctx.trace_id, "032x"),
        "span_id": format(ctx.span_id, "016x"),
        "parent_id": format(s.parent.span_id, "016x") if s.parent else None,
        "start_ns": s.start_time,
        "end_ns": s.end_time,
        "status": {"code": s.status.status_code.name, "description": s.status.description},
        "scope": s.instrumentation_scope.name if s.instrumentation_scope else None,
        "attributes": {k: _value(v) for k, v in (s.attributes or {}).items()},
        "events": [{"name": e.name, "attributes": {k: _value(v) for k, v in (e.attributes or {}).items()}} for e in s.events],
    }


def _versions(library: str) -> dict[str, str | None]:
    out: dict[str, str | None] = {}
    for dist in VERSIONED[library]:
        try:
            out[dist] = metadata.version(dist)
        except metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
            out[dist] = None
    return out


def run(library: str, scenario_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    scenario = get(scenario_id)
    logging.disable(logging.CRITICAL)
    exporter, flush = SETUPS[library]()
    app_fn = APPS[scenario.app]
    with FakeProvider() as fake:
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        try:
            result = app_fn(fake.base_url, scenario.model)
            app = {"outcome": "ok", "result": result}
        except BaseException as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - the outcome is the data
            app = {
                "outcome": "exception",
                "exception_type": type(e).__name__,
                "exception_module": type(e).__module__,
                "message": str(e)[:500],
            }
        app["seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - t0, 3)
        # Let streams closed by garbage collection end their spans.
        gc.collect()
        flush()
        fake_log = fake.log.entries()
    spans = [span_to_dict(s) for s in exporter.get_finished_spans()]
    t = truth.derive(fake_log, app)
    return {
        "truth": {
            **t,
            "scenario": scenario_id,
            "expected": scenario.expected,
            "expected_mismatch": truth.check_expected(scenario.expected, t),
            "app": app,
            "fake_log": fake_log,
        },
        "trace": {"library": library, "versions": _versions(library), "spans": spans},
    }


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    library, scenario_id, out_path = argv
    try:
        payload = {"ok": True, "observation": run(library, scenario_id)}
    except BaseException:  # noqa: BLE001 - reported as NOT RUN by the parent
        payload = {"ok": False, "error": traceback.format_exc(limit=8)}
    with open(out_path, "w") as f:
        json.dump(payload, f, default=str)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
"""Each target library's recommended setup, wired to an in-memory exporter.

Runs inside the child process, in the library's own venv. Each setup returns
the InMemorySpanExporter and a flush function.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Callable

# Environment for every child. Content capture on, all outbound telemetry off.
CHILD_ENV = {
    "OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT": "true",
    "TRACELOOP_TRACE_CONTENT": "true",
    "TRACELOOP_TELEMETRY": "false",
    # A neatlogs exporter pointed at a dead endpoint retries for ~200 s per run.
    "NEATLOGS_DISABLE_EXPORT": "true",
    "OTEL_SDK_DISABLED": "false",
    "OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER": "none",
    "OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER": "none",
    "OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER": "none",
    "OPENAI_API_KEY": "trueup-fake",
    "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "trueup-fake",
}
# Env vars removed from the child so no real key or endpoint is ever used.
CHILD_ENV_DROP = (
    "NEATLOGS_API_KEY",
    "NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT",
    "TRACELOOP_API_KEY",
    "TRACELOOP_BASE_URL",
    "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT",
    "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT",
    "OPENAI_BASE_URL",
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL",
)

# Packages per library venv.
PACKAGES: dict[str, list[str]] = {
    "neatlogs": ["neatlogs", "openai", "anthropic", "opentelemetry-sdk"],
    "openinference": [
        "openinference-instrumentation-openai",
        "openinference-instrumentation-anthropic",
        "openai",
        "anthropic",
        "opentelemetry-sdk",
    ],
    # traceloop-sdk imports httpx without declaring it; openai no longer pulls it in.
    "openllmetry": ["traceloop-sdk", "httpx", "openai", "anthropic"],
}
# Distributions whose versions are recorded with each observation.
VERSIONED: dict[str, list[str]] = {
    "neatlogs": ["neatlogs", "openai", "anthropic", "opentelemetry-sdk"],
    "openinference": [
        "openinference-instrumentation-openai",
        "openinference-instrumentation-anthropic",
        "openai",
        "anthropic",
        "opentelemetry-sdk",
    ],

        "opentelemetry-instrumentation-anthropic",
        "openai",
        "anthropic",
        "opentelemetry-sdk",
    ],
}
LIBRARIES = tuple(PACKAGES)


def neatlogs_init_kwargs(tracer_provider: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """neatlogs.init arguments. Export is off and no endpoint is given."""
    return {
        "api_key": "trueup-fake",
        "instrumentations": ["openai", "anthropic"],
        "disable_export": True,
        "tracer_provider": tracer_provider,
        "register_shutdown_handlers": False,
    }


def setup_neatlogs():
    import neatlogs
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter

    exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
    provider = TracerProvider()
    neatlogs.init(**neatlogs_init_kwargs(provider))
    # Added after init so we see spans after neatlogs' own processor ran.
    provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter))

    def flush() -> None:
        neatlogs.flush(timeout_millis=5000)
        provider.force_flush(5000)

    return exporter, flush


def setup_openinference():
    from openinference.instrumentation.anthropic import AnthropicInstrumentor
    from openinference.instrumentation.openai import OpenAIInstrumentor
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import SimpleSpanProcessor
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter

    exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
    provider = TracerProvider()
    provider.add_span_processor(SimpleSpanProcessor(exporter))
    OpenAIInstrumentor().instrument(tracer_provider=provider)
    AnthropicInstrumentor().instrument(tracer_provider=provider)
    return exporter, lambda: provider.force_flush(5000)


def setup_openllmetry():
    from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export.in_memory_span_exporter import InMemorySpanExporter
    from traceloop.sdk import Traceloop

    exporter = InMemorySpanExporter()
    Traceloop.init(app_name="trueup", exporter=exporter, disable_batch=True, telemetry_enabled=False)

    def flush() -> None:
        from opentelemetry import trace

        p = trace.get_tracer_provider()
        if hasattr(p, "force_flush"):
            p.force_flush(5000)

    return exporter, flush


SETUPS: dict[str, Callable[[], tuple[Any, Callable[[], None]]]] = {
    "neatlogs": setup_neatlogs,
    "openinference": setup_openinference,
    "openllmetry": setup_openllmetry,
}
"""Per-library venvs under .trueup/venvs/<lib>, built with uv."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path

from trueup.runner.setups import PACKAGES

STAMP = "trueup-packages.json"


class VenvError(RuntimeError):
    pass


def venv_dir(root: Path, library: str) -> Path:
    return root.resolve() / ".trueup" / "venvs" / library


def python_path(root: Path, library: str) -> Path:
    return venv_dir(root, library) / "bin" / "python"


def is_ready(root: Path, library: str) -> bool:
    stamp = venv_dir(root, library) / STAMP
    if not stamp.exists() or not python_path(root, library).exists():
        return False
    try:
        return json.loads(stamp.read_text()) == PACKAGES[library]
    except ValueError:
        return False


def ensure(root: Path, library: str, timeout: float = 900) -> Path:
    """Create the venv if missing or out of date. Returns its python."""
    if library not in PACKAGES:
        raise VenvError(f"unknown library {library!r}")
    py = python_path(root, library)
    if is_ready(root, library):
        return py
    uv = shutil.which("uv")
    if uv is None:
        raise VenvError("uv not found on PATH")
    d = venv_dir(root, library)
    d.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    steps = [
        [uv, "venv", "--quiet", "--allow-existing", "--python", "3.12", str(d)],
        [uv, "pip", "install", "--quiet", "--python", str(py), *PACKAGES[library]],
    ]
    for cmd in steps:
        try:
            p = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            raise VenvError(f"timed out: {' '.join(cmd[:3])}") from None
        if p.returncode != 0:
            raise VenvError(f"{' '.join(cmd[:3])} failed: {(p.stderr or p.stdout).strip()[-500:]}")
    (d / STAMP).write_text(json.dumps(PACKAGES[library]))
    return py

"""Where each tracing library keeps the facts the comparer needs. Pure, data-driven.

One Adapter per library. Each names the attribute keys (or key patterns) for:
which spans are LLM calls, tokens, finish reasons, output text, refusals and
tool calls. Two shapes exist: flat attributes with numeric indexes
(neatlogs, OpenInference) and one JSON attribute holding the output messages
(OpenLLMetry's gen_ai.output.messages).

Adding a library means adding one Adapter here, not changing the comparer.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any

# Finish reasons with the same meaning, mapped to one name. OpenLLMetry
# normalises to the OTel GenAI names (stop, tool_call, length); the providers
# and the other libraries keep the raw ones.
FINISH_SYNONYMS = {
    "end_turn": "stop",
    "stop_sequence": "stop",
    "completed": "stop",
    "tool_calls": "tool_call",
    "tool_use": "tool_call",
    "function_call": "tool_call",
    "max_tokens": "length",
    "incomplete": "length",
}


def norm_finish(value: str | None) -> str | None:
    return None if value is None else FINISH_SYNONYMS.get(value, value)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Adapter:
    library: str
    # A span is an LLM call if attributes[key] is in values (any value if values is empty).
    llm_kind: tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]]

    output_tokens: tuple[str, ...]

# Reasoning text is not output text. OpenInference marks it per content part.
_OI_REASONING = re.compile(r"(llm\.output_messages\.\d+\.message\.contents\.\d+)\.message_content\.text")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SpanFacts:
    """What one LLM span says, in the comparer's terms."""

    input_tokens: int | None
    output_tokens: int | None
    response_id: str | None
    finish: tuple[str, ...]
    texts: tuple[str, ...]
    refusals: tuple[str, ...]
    tool_calls: tuple[tuple[str, Any], ...]  # (name, arguments as recorded)


def _first(attrs: dict[str, Any], keys: tuple[str, ...]) -> Any:
    for k in keys:
        if attrs.get(k) is not None:
            return attrs[k]
    return None


def _matching(attrs: dict[str, Any], patterns: tuple[str, ...]) -> list[tuple[re.Match[str], Any]]:
    out = []
    for p in patterns:
        rx = re.compile(p)
        out += [(m, v) for k, v in attrs.items() if (m := rx.fullmatch(k))]
    return out


def _int(v: Any) -> int | None:
    try:
        return int(v)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None


def is_llm_span(adapter: Adapter, span: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    key, values = adapter.llm_kind
    v = span.get("attributes", {}).get(key)
    return v is not None and (not values or v in values)


def _flat_outputs(adapter: Adapter, attrs: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], list[tuple[str, Any]]]:
    texts = []
    for m, v in _matching(attrs, adapter.text):
        rm = _OI_REASONING.fullmatch(m.group(0))
        if rm and attrs.get(f"{rm.group(1)}.message_content.type") == "reasoning":
            continue
        if isinstance(v, str):
            texts.append(v)
    refusals = [v for _, v in _matching(attrs, adapter.refusal) if isinstance(v, str)]
    args = {m.group(1): v for m, v in _matching(attrs, adapter.tool_args)}
    tools = [(v, args.get(m.group(1))) for m, v in _matching(attrs, adapter.tool_name)]
    return texts, refusals, tools


def _json_outputs(raw: Any) -> tuple[list[str], list[str], list[tuple[str, Any]]]:
    texts: list[str] = []
    refusals: list[str] = []
    tools: list[tuple[str, Any]] = []
    try:
        messages = json.loads(raw) if isinstance(raw, str) else (raw or [])
    except ValueError:
        return texts, refusals, tools
    for msg in messages if isinstance(messages, list) else []:
        for part in (msg or {}).get("parts", []) if isinstance(msg, dict) else []:
            kind = part.get("type")
            if kind == "text" and isinstance(part.get("content"), str):
                texts.append(part["content"])
            elif kind == "refusal" and isinstance(part.get("content"), str):
                refusals.append(part["content"])
            elif kind == "tool_call":
                tools.append((part.get("name"), part.get("arguments")))
    return texts, refusals, tools


def _finish(adapter: Adapter, attrs: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, ...]:
    out: list[str] = []
    for _, v in _matching(attrs, adapter.finish):
        for x in v if isinstance(v, list) else [v]:
            if isinstance(x, str) and x:
                out.append(x)
    return tuple(out)


def facts(adapter: Adapter, span: dict[str, Any]) -> SpanFacts:
    attrs = span.get("attributes", {})
    if adapter.messages_json:
        texts, refusals, tools = _json_outputs(attrs.get(adapter.messages_json))
    else:
        texts, refusals, tools = _flat_outputs(adapter, attrs)
    rid = _first(attrs, adapter.response_id)
    return SpanFacts(
        input_tokens=_int(_first(attrs, adapter.input_tokens)),
        output_tokens=_int(_first(attrs, adapter.output_tokens)),
        response_id=rid if isinstance(rid, str) else None,
        finish=_finish(adapter, attrs),
        texts=tuple(texts),
        refusals=tuple(refusals),
        tool_calls=tuple(tools),
    )

"""Leads table and leads.json payload. Pure: returns strings and dicts."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections import Counter
from typing import Any

from trueup.core.model import Mismatch, Severity

COLUMNS = ("scenario", "check", "expected", "actual", "severity")
CELL_MAX = 48


def _cell(v: Any) -> str:
    s = v if isinstance(v, str) else json.dumps(v, default=str)
    return s if len(s) <= CELL_MAX else s[: CELL_MAX - 3] + "..."


def rows(by_scenario: list[tuple[str, list[Mismatch]]]) -> list[tuple[str, ...]]:
    out = []
    for sid, ms in by_scenario:
        for m in sorted(ms, key=lambda m: -m.severity.rank):
            check = m.check if m.kind == "lead" else f"{m.check} (note)"
            out.append((sid, check, _cell(m.truth), _cell(m.trace), m.severity.value.upper()))
    return out


def table(by_scenario: list[tuple[str, list[Mismatch]]]) -> str:
    body = rows(by_scenario)
    if not body:
        return "no leads"
    widths = [max(len(r[i]) for r in [COLUMNS, *body]) for i in range(len(COLUMNS))]
    line = lambda r: "  ".join(c.ljust(w) for c, w in zip(r, widths)).rstrip()  # noqa: E731
    return "\n".join([line(COLUMNS), line(tuple("-" * w for w in widths)), *(line(r) for r in body)])


def counts(by_scenario: list[tuple[str, list[Mismatch]]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    leads = [m for _, ms in by_scenario for m in ms if m.kind == "lead"]
    notes = [m for _, ms in by_scenario for m in ms if m.kind == "note"]
    sev = Counter(m.severity.value for m in leads)
    return {
        "leads": len(leads),
        "notes": len(notes),
        "by_severity": {s.value: sev.get(s.value, 0) for s in sorted(Severity, reverse=True)},
        "by_check": dict(sorted(Counter(m.check for m in leads).items())),
        "scenarios_with_leads": sum(any(m.kind == "lead" for m in ms) for _, ms in by_scenario),
    }


def leads_payload(run_id: str, library: str, by_scenario: list[tuple[str, list[Mismatch]]],
                  not_run: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "run_id": run_id,
        "library": library,
        "note": "A lead is a disagreement between truth and trace. It is not a confirmed bug.",
        "counts": counts(by_scenario),
        "not_run": not_run,
        "scenarios": [{"scenario": sid, "mismatches": [m.to_dict() for m in ms]} for sid, ms in by_scenario],
    }

"""trueup audit <agent.py>: run a user's main() against the fake under one tracing library.

How it works:
  1. Run main() once with plain replies, to see which provider routes it calls.
  2. For each route it called, run main() once per fake scenario on that route
     (errors, cuts, tools, refusal, ...). Other routes keep plain replies.
  3. Compare truth (the fake's log and main()'s outcome) with the spans.

Limits:
  - main() must take no arguments and reach the provider through the openai or
    anthropic SDK, with clients that read OPENAI_BASE_URL / ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL
    (the default). A client with a hard-coded base_url is not redirected.
  - It runs in the library's venv, which has only the tracing library, openai
    and anthropic. A script that needs other packages will not import.
  - The fake answers every call on a route the same way. Agent loops that wait
    for a particular reply may stop early or loop until their own limit.
  - SDK retries are real requests: with the default max_retries a 500 is sent
    three times, and the call count check compares against all of them.
  - There is no scenario expectation, so the "library changed the request"
    note is not produced, and an app that stops reading a stream early is not
    detected (its output is still expected on the span).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Callable

from trueup.core import report
from trueup.core.compare import compare
from trueup.core.model import Observation
from trueup.fake.server import SCENARIOS_BY_ROUTE
from trueup.runner import RAN, venvs
from trueup.runner.run import not_run, run_audit
from trueup.sweep import by_scenario, new_run_id, summary_line

DISCOVER = "discover"


def audit(
    root: Path,
    library: str,
    script: Path,
    *,
    ensure: Callable[[Path, str], Path] = venvs.ensure,
    run: Callable[..., dict[str, Any]] = run_audit,
    out: Callable[[str], None] = print,
) -> tuple[Path, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    run_id = new_run_id(library).replace(f"-{library}", f"-audit-{library}")
    run_dir = root / ".trueup" / "runs" / run_id
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    results: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    if not script.is_file():
        results.append(not_run(DISCOVER, library, f"no such file: {script}"))
    else:
        try:
            out(f"preparing venv for {library}")
            python = ensure(root, library)
        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 - reported as could not run
            python = None
            results.append(not_run(DISCOVER, library, f"venv not ready: {e}"))
        if python is not None:
            results = _audit_runs(python, library, script, run, out)
    for r in results:
        name = r["scenario"].replace("/", "_")
        (run_dir / f"{name}.json").write_text(json.dumps(r, indent=1, default=str))
    by = by_scenario(results)
    table = report.table(by)
    c = report.counts(by)
    not_run_list = [{"scenario": r["scenario"], "reason": r["reason"]} for r in results if r["status"] != RAN]
    (run_dir / "leads.json").write_text(json.dumps(report.leads_payload(run_id, library, by, not_run_list),
                                                   indent=1, default=str))
    (run_dir / "summary.txt").write_text("\n".join([
        f"trueup audit {script} --library {library}  run {run_id}",
        f"leads: {c['leads']}  by severity: {c['by_severity']}",
        "A lead is a disagreement between truth and trace, not a confirmed bug.",
        "",
        *(summary_line(r) for r in results),
        "",
        table,
    ]) + "\n")
    out("")
    out(table)
    out(f"leads: {c['leads']}  by severity: {c['by_severity']}; wrote {run_dir}")
    return run_dir, results


def _audit_runs(python: Path, library: str, script: Path, run: Callable[..., dict[str, Any]],
                out: Callable[[str], None]) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    first = run(python, library, script, DISCOVER, {})
    out(summary_line(first))
    if first["status"] != RAN:
        return [first]
    routes = sorted({e["path"] for e in first["observation"]["truth"]["fake_log"]} & set(SCENARIOS_BY_ROUTE))
    if not routes:
        return [not_run(DISCOVER, library, "main() made no provider call through the fake "
                        "(check that its clients use OPENAI_BASE_URL / ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL)")]
    out(f"main() calls: {', '.join(routes)}")
    results = []
    for route in routes:
        for scenario in SCENARIOS_BY_ROUTE[route]:
            r = run(python, library, script, scenario, {route: scenario})
            if r["status"] == RAN:
                r["mismatches"] = [m.to_dict() for m in compare(Observation.from_dict(r["observation"]))]
            out(summary_line(r))
            results.append(r)
    return results

content.text:
The comparer, the leads report, `sweep` comparing, and `audit` are all built. I re-ran the sweeps for all three libraries one at a time, and each ran 31/31. Nothing is committed.

**Tests:** `uv run pytest -q` gives 155 passed, 12 e2e deselected. I also ran the new e2e audit test for openinference only, and it passed. I didn't run it for neatlogs or openllmetry, and I didn't run the full e2e suite.

**Leads per library** (leads, not confirmed bugs):

| library | high | medium | low | total leads | notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| neatlogs | 4 | 18 | 0 | 22 | 5 |
| openinference | 2 | 8 | 0 | 10 | 0 |
| openllmetry | 11 | 3 | 0 | 14 | 0 |

- **neatlogs:** spans from Anthropic `messages.stream` have no tokens, text, tool calls or finish reason. Responses spans have no status or finish reason, and two have no function calls. The chat refusal isn't recorded. The Responses stream that ends with an error event stays UNSET. The 5 notes are neatlogs adding `stream_options.include_usage`; tokens are checked against what the fake really sent.
- **openinference:** there's no span for a chat stream closed early, or for a Responses stream that ends with an error event. Responses spans have no status or finish reason, and the chat refusal isn't recorded.
- **openllmetry:** chat streams that raised, and the Responses error-event stream, end as OK. Some calls have no span at all: Responses failed/incomplete and Anthropic stream errors/cuts. Anthropic streamed spans show 4 output tokens where the provider sent 3.

The counts per check are in `hackathon.md`.

**What changed:**
- **Comparer:** `src/trueup/core/compare.py` applies the seven checks plus the LOW "library changed the request" note. It's pure code with no I/O.
- **Adapters:** `src/trueup/core/adapters.py` has one data-driven adapter per library. They're tested against 21 trimmed span samples in `tests/fixtures/spans/`. I removed stack traces, local URLs and paths from them and found no secrets.
- **Report:** `src/trueup/core/report.py` builds the leads table and `leads.json`.
- **`sweep`:** now compares and prints the table. It exits 1 if any lead, otherwise 2 if any scenario couldn't run, otherwise 0. If some scenarios fail to run and others have leads, it exits 1.
- **`audit`:** `trueup audit <script> --library <lib>` (in `src/trueup/audit.py`) first runs `main()` once to see which provider routes it calls. It then runs `main()` once per fake scenario on those routes and compares. To make this work, the fake can now be told which scenario to answer with on a route, whatever model name the app sends. On `examples/agent.py` under openinference it made 8 runs and found 1 lead (the refusal isn't recorded).
- **Docs:** `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and `hackathon.md` are updated.

**Calls I made that you may want to review:**
- Finish reasons are compared through a table of equivalent names (`end_turn` = `stop`, `tool_use` = `tool_call`, `incomplete` = `length`), because OpenLLMetry renames them.
- When the app closes a stream early, output, tokens and finish aren't compared, because the app never received them.
- Missing spans are counted under "span closed" and extra spans under "call count", so a missing span isn't counted twice.
- OpenLLMetry's span for a failed stream has no operation name, so its adapter identifies LLM spans by `gen_ai.provider.name` instead.

**Not done, or limited:**
- `audit` can't tell when an app stops reading a stream early, and it can't produce the "request changed" note, because a user's script has no expected results.
- SDK retries count as separate requests in `audit`, so a script using the default retries can show call-count leads.
- `audit` only works with the packages already in the library's environment.
- Framework scenarios are still not built. The self-check of the leads comes next.

These limits are written down in `src/trueup/audit.py`.
